title: Subject-Verb Agreement Applied
subtitle: Amounts, titles, and nouns that lie about their number.
objectives: Use singular verbs with amounts treated as one unit
Use singular verbs with titles of works
Identify nouns that look plural but are singular
Identify nouns that are always plural
Distinguish a number of from the number of
Retell the episode with the sheep

cards.title: Some nouns end in -s and are perfectly singular
cards.text: News. Mathematics. Physics. All of them end in -s and every one of them takes a singular verb.

cards.title: Looks plural, is singular
cards.text: These are subjects and topics. Ignore the -s completely and treat each one as a single thing.

cards.title: Always plural, and there is no singular form
cards.text: These are things made of two joined halves. You cannot have one trouser, and the verb is always plural.
points: **Say "a pair of"** and it becomes singular.
**"A pair of scissors *is* blunt."** Pair is the subject now.

question.explain: Mathematics ends in -s but is one subject. It takes a singular verb.

cards.title: A quantity acting as one thing is singular
cards.text: When money, distance, time or weight is being treated as a single amount, the verb is singular.

cards.title: "Three rounds is not a fight"
cards.text: Nobody says three rounds are not a fight. You are talking about one stretch of time, not three separate things.
points: **"The three rounds *were* all close."** Different meaning.
**Ask that**, and the verb chooses itself.

options: Twenty kilometres is a long run
Twenty kilometres are a long run
Twenty kilometre is a long run
Twenty kilometres were a long run
question.explain: It is one distance, treated as a single amount, so the verb is singular.

cards.title: Good spot to pause
cards.text: Amounts done. Part 2 is titles, the number rule, and the sheep. Your place is saved.

cards.eyebrow: Part 2 · Titles and the number rule
cards.title: A book with a plural title is still one book
cards.text: "The Avengers is a long film." It sounds wrong the first time and it is correct every time.

cards.title: The title of a work is one thing
cards.text: Books, films, songs and games take singular verbs however plural their titles look.
points: **Trust the rule** over your ear here.

cards.title: "Halo Infinite is out"
cards.text: A game title is a single work. Even if the title is plural, the game is one thing and takes a singular verb.
points: **Same for a band's album**, and a film.

options: The Lord of the Rings is a long book
The Lord of the Rings are a long book
The Lord of the Rings were long books
The Lord of the Ring are long
question.explain: A title names one work. However plural it looks, the verb is singular.

cards.title: A number of, and the number of
cards.text: One word different, and the verb flips. This is the most precise rule in the whole topic.
points: ***The number* is one figure**, and figures are singular.

question.text: Complete it: "The number of entries ___ increased."
question.explain: The number is one figure, so it takes a singular verb. "A number of entries have" would be plural.

cards.title: The Adventure with the Sheep
cards.text: Two clouds of dust rise on the road ahead. Don Quixote announces that they are two great armies about to meet in battle.

cards.title: He names the knights on both sides
cards.text: He describes the champions of each army in enormous detail. Their shields, their devices, the lands they rule.
points: **The detail is what makes it funny.**
**Sancho says he can hear only sheep.**
**Don Quixote says fear is affecting his hearing.**

cards.title: The shepherds fight back
cards.text: He charges into the flock and starts killing sheep. The shepherds bring him down with stones from their slings.
points: **He loses several teeth** and cracks ribs.
**The shepherds carry off their dead sheep.**
**Sancho counts the cost** in animals and money.
**And Don Quixote blames the enchanter.** Again.

cards.title: The detail is the joke, not the mistake
cards.text: Anyone can mistake dust for an army. Inventing forty named knights with heraldry is what makes the scene work.
points: **He is not confused.** He is elaborating.

question.text: Don Quixote accepts that the armies were sheep after the shepherds knock him down.
question.explain: False. He blames the enchanter for turning the armies into sheep, exactly as with the windmills.

terms.def: Money, time or distance treated as a single quantity. Takes a singular verb.
A book, film or game is one work, so the verb is singular.
News, mathematics, physics. They end in -s and are singular.
Scissors, trousers, glasses. No singular form, and always a plural verb.
Means several. Takes a plural verb.
Names one figure. Takes a singular verb.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **An amount as one unit is singular.**
**A number of = plural. The number of = singular.**

options: The news is on at nine
The news are on at nine
The news were on at nine
The new is on at nine

quiz.text: Complete it: "A number of students ___ waiting outside."
quiz.explain: 'A number of' means several, so the verb is plural.
quiz.objective: Distinguish a number of from the number of

quiz.text: Complete it: "The number of students ___ growing."
quiz.explain: 'The number' is one figure. One word different from the last question, opposite verb.

quiz.text: What does Don Quixote take the two dust clouds to be?
quiz.explain: Two armies, and he describes the champions of both sides in detail. They are flocks of sheep.

quiz.text: How does the sheep episode end for Don Quixote?
options: The shepherds knock him down with slingstones and he loses teeth
He drives the flock away successfully
quiz.explain: He kills several sheep before the shepherds bring him down. He blames the enchanter afterwards.
quiz.objective: Retell the episode with the sheep

teacher.summary: Week 10 English completes subject-verb agreement with the cases that defeat a good ear, and closes the Don Quixote strand for the term. Everything here is a noun that misreports its own number: subjects ending in -s that are singular, tools made of two halves that are always plural, amounts that act as one unit, and titles that name one work. The a-number-of against the-number-of pair is the most precise rule in the topic and is worth the card it gets. The sheep episode is chosen to end on because it shows the pattern of the whole book at its clearest: the mistake is ordinary, and the elaborate invented detail on top of it is what makes it Don Quixote. NOTE ON THE TEXT: the school's edition is abridged and does not follow Cervantes' chapter numbering.
discussion: Ask him to say 'The Avengers is a long film' out loud. It sounds wrong and it is right, which is worth sitting with.
Ask what changes between 'a number of' and 'the number of'. One word, opposite verb.
Ask why 'ten pesos is' rather than 'are'. One amount rather than ten separate coins.
Ask what makes the sheep scene funny. Mistaking dust for an army is ordinary; naming forty knights is not.
teacher.extension: Have him write ten sentences using the nouns from this lesson — news, scissors, mathematics, a pair of, ten pesos, a title — and check each verb. These are the ones a good ear gets wrong.
misconceptions: 'Anything ending in -s is plural.' News, mathematics and physics are all singular.
'Scissors can be singular if there is one pair.' The noun stays plural. Say 'a pair of scissors' and pair becomes the subject.
'A plural title takes a plural verb.' A title names one work and takes a singular verb.
'A number of and the number of are the same.' They take opposite verbs, and the exam knows it.
